sources.citation: Roberts, John R. 1997. Switch-reference in Papua New Guinea: a preliminary survey. In Andrew Pawley (ed.), Papers in Papuan Linguistics No. 3, 101-241. Pacific Linguistics A-87. Canberra: Australian National University. doi:10.15144/PL-A87.101
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'In the Nuru family SSIDS is reported to occur in the Erima language. For the Usu, Duduela, Kwato, Rerau, Jilim, and Yangulam languages there is no information available as to whether they have SSIDS or not.'; appendix row 'Usu, Duduela, Kwato, Rerau, Jilim, Yangulam: no information available'. Typological survey of switch-reference morphology; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xvi+196 pp. doi:10.15144/PL-D30
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction sec. 7 (pp. vii-viii): 'semiphonemic' transcription and a sound-fluctuation table (Usu: dz ~ z, z ~ y); no mention of stress/accent. Only prosodic remark in the volume is note 3 p.172 'the Dumpu-Watiwa language is tonal' (B5, not Usu). B18 Usu wordlist entries carry vowel length and glottal stop but no stress marks (checked page images, printed pp. 16 and 101).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (PL C-38), 569-612. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.8.2.2.1.1.5 (p.581) lists the Nuru Family (Usu, Erima, Duduela, Kwato, Rerau, Jilim, Yangulam) and notes Usu 'was pushed further south.. by the Ham people'; population B18 Usu 93; pronoun/lexical tables only; the words stress/tone/suprasegmental do not occur in the chapter.
